ranges.quote: Here's the problem. Models can't eat raw text, and letter by letter is too slow to learn from. Whole words means a vocabulary of millions, and one typo becomes an unknown word.

ranges.quote: So a tokenizer chops text into tokens, chunks somewhere between letters and words. Common words stay whole. Rarer ones will split straw and berry.
ranges.reason: The earlier ~49.36 take is a false start -- this is the keeper. ASR boxes 'So' 61.70-62.04; acoustic onset is 61.61, start padded to 61.52. ranges.quote: The model never receives letters at all. It receives token ID numbers, so asking it to count letters is like asking you to count letters in a word you've only ever heard spoken.
